key_insight: ERCPMP-Gx introduces a dataset that connects endoscopic images and videos of colorectal polyposis with richer clinical labels, moving beyond single-polyp datasets. This enables AI models to study polyposis at the syndrome level, not just the lesion level.
problem_solved: Public endoscopy datasets are mostly built around isolated sporadic polyps and do not link visible morphology to histopathology or genomic context. This makes it difficult to train AI systems for accurate hereditary polyposis classification and early risk stratification.
method: Curate an endoscopic image/video dataset focused on colorectal polyposis cases.
Associate visual findings with morphological, histopathological, and genomic information.
Provide a research resource for classification, characterization, and downstream AI model development.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this dataset supports multimodal learning and clinically meaningful classification tasks that are closer to real-world diagnosis. It can improve model generalization for hereditary cancer risk assessment and precision surveillance workflows.

paper_title: ERCPMP-Gx: Endoscopic Image and Video Dataset for Morphological, Histopathological, and Genomic Characterization of Colorectal Polyposis
paper_authors: Zahra Ghaffari, Massih Bahar, Mojgan Forootan, Ali Darvishi, Hamidreza Bolhasani
